environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with EU Directive 2010/75/EU for industrial emissions; wastewater discharge limits per French environmental code (e.g., <50 mg/L BOD for treated effluent)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) of the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery, with the electronic filing portal at impots.gouv.fr and business registration portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT operational matters are handled by the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and interregional DGFiP VAT units.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must complete statutory business formation or branch registration via the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), obtaining the SIREN registration number and SIRET establishment number. The SIREN serves as the French tax identification number. For VAT purposes, the DGFiP assigns a French intra-Community VAT number (FR followed by the INSEE key and SIREN) once the business registration file is transmitted. A foreign company not established in France and not required to register through the Guichet Unique must file Form FI? or Form 5466? alternative online application for direct VAT registration with the competent DGFiP VAT service. If the foreign entity has no permanent establishment in France, it must generally appoint an individual tax representative approved by DGFiP who is jointly and severally liable for French tax, or use the non-EU simplified distance selling registration procedure where applicable. Bank account powers of attorney, confirmation of legal existence, local address or representative mandate, and certified translation of constitutional documents are required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SARL is by default liable to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Article 206 of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI). The territoriality scope for IS covers the worldwide profits of French-established SARLs, subject to tax treaties on non-French source profits through neutralization or permanent establishment analysis; profits of foreign branches are assessed in France if not allocated to a foreign PE, with tax credits available. Under narrow statutory conditions, a family SARL may elect partial taxation at the partner level as a transparent partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime comparable to the US IRS. Identified statutory election mechanisms include: (i) the option for a SARL whose shares are continuously held by individuals and which qualifies as a 'family SARL' to be taxed under Article 239 quater CGI on the income tax scale of the partners, subject to revocation within a time limit; (ii) the option under Article 239 nonies for certain services enterprises to be treated similarly; (iii) the election under Article 206-2 to renounce corporate income tax for collective civil entities?; and refusal of extension to hybrid entities. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD are transposed through Articles 212-1 bis? and 212-1 ter? of the CGI, requiring classification consistency between France and the foreign jurisdiction; mismatches may give rise to mandatory denial of deductions or inclusion of with-in cash amounts. Any election concerning transparent treatment must be filed with the local SIE within the tax return deadline for the relevant fiscal year and is binding until formally abandoned.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA), governed by Articles 256 to 283 CGI and Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For taxable persons established in France there is no general registration threshold; any VATable supply obligates registration. For non-established EU suppliers of distance sales of goods, the pan-European EUR 10,000 threshold applies for determining whether French VAT is declared at destination. Non-EU suppliers have no threshold and are taxable from the first supply unless the reverse charge or invoicing through a fiscal representative applies. A French fixed establishment, permanent warehouse, or stocked consignment creates full registration status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G invoicing is already mandatorily electronic via Chorus Pro. The national e-invoicing reform introduces mandatory structured B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting through certified 'Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires' (PDP) or a public portal, with PDF no longer valid for domestic B2B transactions. Factures must be transmitted in structured formats (EN16931/Peppol BIS, JSON/XML cross-industry invoice) through a registered PDP providing cryptographic integrity, electronic signature, and unique invoice numbering. Reporting data is cleared by the PDP to DGFiP at transactional level in near real-time; no live-animation fiscal stamping similar to Latin America is applied. The obligation enters into force progressively on 1 September 2026 and is completed by 1 September 2027; interim annual and periodical VAT statements remain mandatory for export and offshore supply proofs.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Sales of movable goods qualify for the 0% French export VAT rate under Article 262-1 CGI only where the vendor supplies goods shipped or transported to a destination outside the European Union by the vendor, by the customer, or on behalf of either, and proof of the physical departure from the EU customs territory is held. The vendor must issue an invoice with a legal mention 'Exportation', keep the customs export declaration (H1 or electronic declaration), transport documents, and evidence of delivery to the non-EU purchaser; the goods must leave the EU within the statutory proof deadline, generally 90 days from invoice date, subject to justified exceptions. Offshore services fall outside the French VAT scope when the place-of-supply rule places the service in the jurisdiction of an overseas customer and the purchaser is a taxable person located outside the EU; for services physically connected to French territory, VAT neutrality may require careful documentation to demonstrate foreign effective use and enjoyment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (H1 or electronic DELTA message) validated by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR road consignment note, Air Waybill (AWB), or multimodal transport document evidencing departure from France to a non-EU customs territory
Commercial invoice matching the export declaration with value, HS/ISIC classification, and military/tactical end-use markings
Proof of the customer's identity and non-EU establishment, including certificate of incorporation or embassy/diplomatic confirmation
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT proof showing settlement by the foreign purchaser
Insurance certificate and packing list enabling cross-checking of the consignment
End-User Certificate and relevant defense export license for ISIC 3040 tactical armored vehicles or controlled goods, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and French Customs jointly scrutinize export zero-rating claims, focusing on fictitious exports, false end-use certificates, circular cargo flows, and deficient documentary files. If the 0% rate is non-conforming, the VAT originally returned or exempted is clawed back, plus interest at 0.20% per month. Article 1729 CGI applies a 40% increase for mauvaise foi (lack of good faith) and an 80% increase for manoeuvres frauduleuses; Article 1728 CGI applies separate late-filing and late-payment increases; Article 1741 CGI criminalizes fraudulent tax evasion with penalties up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment. Customs penalties under the Code des douanes can include seizure of the goods, confiscation of the transport vehicle, and personal liability of the exporter. The ordinary reassessment period is three years, extended to six years in cases involving undisclosed foreign activities or passive receipts, and to ten years for organized tax fraud; retrospective cancellations are accompanied by revocation of export licenses and referral to the Directorate General for Armaments for illicit defense-trade procurement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France; the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) exercises banking licensing and AML supervision, while the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) administers exchange control, FDI and defense-sector screening, and financial sanctions in the French Republic.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is full legal tender in France; current-account payments are freely convertible for EU/EEA counterparties and generally liberalised for non-EU counterparties under Articles L151-1 to L151-5 of the Code monétaire et financier. Capital-account movements are fully liberalised within the EU, but a non-EU foreign direct investment into an ISIC 3040 armored tactical vehicle manufacturer triggers Decree No. 2019-1590 and the EU FDI screening Regulation; prior Ministerial approval is required before any non-EU investor acquires a controlling stake or provides related funding. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation are legally unrestricted after the SARL's annual financial statements are approved and French withholding-tax/dividend formalities have been completed; the practical obstacles are not exchange-conversion limits but the bank's sanctions screening of beneficial owners seated in non-cooperative jurisdictions. France does not distinguish between soft and hard currencies in bank practice, but credit institutions may decline payments to or from countries on FATF/EU blacklists unless a derogation is pre-approved by the French Ministry of Economy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no percentage surrender or forced conversion obligation on export proceeds denominated in EUR; the mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0%. For export receivables in a foreign currency, the SARL must collect the receivable within 30 days after the contractual due date, route collection exclusively through an ACPR-licensed French credit institution, and promptly convert or offset the foreign-currency balance into EUR unless a genuine matching FX position exists for trade debt. Every cross-border transfer exceeding EUR 10,000 must be reported monthly to the Banque de France by the French intermediary; late repatriation beyond 30 days must be individually declared and may trigger administrative fines under Articles L161-1 and R161-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for principal treasury use and Medium only for incidental operating expenses. French law permits an ACPR-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution to provide payment accounts; however, offshore digital EMIs without a full EU/EEA passport cannot lawfully service a French defense contractor. The ISIC 3040 armored vehicle scope requires underlying banking products that standard EMIs do not offer: documentary letters of credit, bank guarantees, escrow accounts, government reimbursements and structured trade finance. UK-FCA-only EMIs are non-viable after Brexit because their license no longer passes into France; even EEA-licensed EMIs should only process payroll, per-diem and small sub-supplier payments under EUR 10,000. They must never be used for DGA-licensed export proceeds, inbound capital injections, or diplomatic LC receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview is the normative requirement and is effectively mandatory for the French managing director (Gérant) plus at least one 25%-plus ultimate beneficial owner. Banks allow remote video opening only where the parent shareholder is a regulated EU bank or a listed industrial group already known to the compliance desk. In all other cases attendance at a French branch or corporate centre is required. Non-resident directors must present notarised or apostilled passports, three months of source-of-wealth evidence, and a French fiscal-residence certificate or equivalent tax-treaty attestation. Signatories will be verified against the FICOBA national bank-account file, and the bank may demand a Banque de France professional onboarding confirmation and a live recorded interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity manufactures ISIC 3040 armored security/personnel transport vehicles; the sector is treated as defense-sensitive with automatic dual-use/military-goods flags, embargo checks, and possible Ministerial involvement in account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide DGA (Direction Générale de l’Armement) product-classification letter; EU General Export Authorization or individual export license number; final end-user certificate and signed Statement of Non-Diversion; French customs Binding Tariff Information showing the correct tariff line; and an independent sanctions-screening report confirming no OFAC, EU, UN or DGA-listed parties in the transaction chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered French SARL with no statutory minimum capital and no operating track record creates thin-substance suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered SARL statutes and UBO declaration under Décret n°2021-1626; certified proof of paid-in capital of at least EUR 100,000; audited financial statements or management accounts of the ultimate parent for three years; signed group organigramme; bank reference letter from the parent's prime lender; and the defense-sector business plan incorporating the DGA authorization or a pending application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export corridor involves embassies, ministries, sovereign wealth funds, or procurement agencies in high-risk geographies such as Middle East, North Africa or Southeast Asia, triggering corruption, anti-bribery and arms-embargo scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intergovernmental procurement agreement or State-to-State memorandum of understanding; verified diplomatic or government purchase order and invoice; EU end-use certificate completed by the buyer's Ministry of Defense; strict beneficiary matching to the export license; no split payments; and a legal opinion from a French avocat covering FCPA/UK Bribery Act and intermediary integrity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large non-resident capital injection or sovereign buyer prepayment into an escrow account may be flagged as undisclosed lending, sanctions fronting, or circular payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholder meeting minutes authorising the equity contribution; bank certificate of receipt of funds; transaction reference codes aligned to the capital increase and treasury declaration; signed underlying procurement contract with milestones; treasury declaration for defense export signed by the Gérant; and confirmation that the funds originated from a licensed financial institution and not from cash or virtual-asset convertors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed dividend remittance or shareholder-loan repayment to non-resident UBOs may be interpreted as tax-motivated capital outflow before the export license is physically granted.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved annual financial statements; shareholder dividend resolution; tax-residence certificates for each recipient; underlying loan agreements with arm's-length interest rates registered with the Banque de France where applicable; and a formal French legal opinion that no DGA suspension or authorization condition is currently in force.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a single unbroken SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's bank to the SARL's French IBAN (FR76 format) at BNP Paribas or Société Générale in Paris. The purpose description must distinguish 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION TO SARL CAPITAL INCREASE' from 'CONVERTIBLE SHAREHOLDER LOAN'; generic codes such as 'INVESTMENT' or 'SERVICES' are non-compliant. The wire may only be released after the corporate capital-increase minutes are executed, the notarial or banking deposit certificate is issued, and the Banque de France monthly declaration is prepared. Never split large capital transfers into smaller tranches to avoid reporting thresholds. For non-EU investors in this defense sector, the Ministry of Economy prior-authorisation reference should be quoted in field 70 of the MT103; receipt of funds without that approval is a banking violation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle ordinary trade payables and supplier advances by SWIFT MT103 customer-credit transfer. For government and diplomatic procurement contracts use irrevocable confirmed sight commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 and routed through a prime OECD bank, with reimbursement to Société Générale's trade-finance desk. Drawings must be matched to a French customs export declaration (C21/DEB) and the relevant export-license number. The original transport document must evidence the destination named in the end-user certificate. No trade disbursement may be directed to a commission agent in a third country unless the commission agreement has passed EU export-control due diligence and the agent's KYC file contains a valid passport, proof of address, and no UN/EU/OFC sanctions listing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable spot and outright forward contracts up to 24 months, confirmed with the French account bank or an OECD counterparty and reported under EMIR trade repositories

EUR/USD non-deliverable forward (NDF) with an offshore correspondent, permitted only when the final customer invoice is in a soft or blocked currency and the notional does not exceed the outstanding receivable; cash settlement must be in EUR
EUR/CNY deliverable forward or flexible forward with an ACPR-licensed Chinese/EU bank for imported components and logistics services from the People's Republic of China
EUR/AED and EUR/SAR cross-currency swaps for netting of export proceeds from Gulf Cooperation Council defense procurement programmes
European-style EUR/USD currency options, with premium denominated in EUR, used strictly to hedge bid exposure before contract award; leveraged or exotic options are prohibited

Synthetic FX netting through a multi-currency treasury account: matching foreign-currency inflows against existing foreign-currency payables reduces the need for separate hedging trades, provided the net open FX position does not exceed EUR 5,000,000 and the bank's ALM policy is fully documented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting approval of annual accounts (procès-verbal d'assemblée générale ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a regulator; minutes retained in the statutory minute book at the registered office and made available to auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The shareholders' meeting to approve annual accounts must be convened within six months after the close of the financial year (Art. L.223-26 C. com.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve the accounts exposes SARL managers to criminal fines up to EUR 9,000 (Art. L.241-2 C. com.); the court may appoint an agent to convene the meeting at the manager's expense, and losses not approved may not be carried forward for tax purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office département; publication in BODACC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; approval must occur within six months of the balance-sheet date, producing a maximum statutory deadline of seven months after financial-year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is punishable by a fine of up to EUR 1,500 for a natural person and EUR 7,500 for a legal entity; the registry may obtain a court order imposing a civil penalty of up to EUR 150 per day of delay; continued non-filing can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and financial schedules (liasse fiscale: form 2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (DGFiP) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; for a staggered year-end, within three months after the close of the financial year (electronic filing mandatory)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an automatic penalty of 5% of the corporate tax due plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%; the absence of a complete return can lead to a summary assessment, and an increase to 10% penalty for unpaid tax after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration and payment of the local business contribution – CFE (déclaration n°1447-C-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (local territorial office) for the registered-office municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration filed by 3 May each year for the renewal year; final payment of the balance by 15 December of the chargeable year unless instalment rules apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment or late filing attracts monthly interest of 0.20% and a 10% late-payment penalty; non-declaration permits the tax administration to assess CFE on a discretionary basis and to initiate distraint proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updated beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) upon ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) through the INPI formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership; French law does not prescribe a separate annual UBO confirmation form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or false declaration is a criminal offence with fines up to EUR 7,500 (natural person) and EUR 15,000 (legal entity); persistent non-compliance may also be treated as a registration-lapse triggering judicial strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory, inter alia, where the SARL exceeds two of the following thresholds at the closing date for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,000,000; net turnover EUR 8,000,000; average workforce 50 employees. Appointment is also required when shareholders holding at least one-tenth of the capital petition the court, in consolidated groups, or when the company is subject to special defence-sector oversight and export-control authorisation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles (Plan Comptable Général / PCG) as incorporated in the Code de commerce; consolidated financial statements may elect IFRS as adopted by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not operate an annual UBO filing cycle. The beneficial-owner statement is filed on incorporation and any shareholding transfer triggers a mandatory update filed with the RCS within 30 days; the register must continuously reflect the share and control structure as of each fiscal year-end.

stage_6.entry_description: Unique SIREN/SIRET identifier, APE/NAF code 3040A? Actually manufacturing of military vehicles: NAF code 30.40 — 3040A / 3040B? Let me note.
